newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrials and all-shares ended a quiet week firmer ahead of the Good Friday and Easter Monday holidays.
"Industrials and all-shares were up, but it's all been pretty quiet which is to be expected," one dealer said.
"We're into holiday season and there are a lot of portfolio managers away," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
Dealers said the rise in industrials and all-shares was poretty much due to window-dressing for the unit-trust close-out on Thursday.
But some commentators added that the underlying tone to the market was positive and, providing U.S. stocks suffered no serious setback, local shares would be safe.
Gold shares finished flat after nudging up slightly.

Dealers said that the index was unlikely to brighten due to expectations that first quarter gold results will be disappointing and the weak bullion price is set to erode interest in gold shares even further.
Shares next week were seen tracking Wall Street which could still be affected by the Federal Reserve's 25 basis point rate hike on Tuesday.
"This market is jittery because of what's happening in the U.S. We'll watch the Dow closely," said Denzil Newman, Syfrets Managed Assets portfolio manager.
"Sentiment about our market is improving. Foreigners are showing reasonable interest," he added.
Shares were unmoved by the February CPI number and trade figure.
Industrials finished up 31.4 points at 8,339.4, all-shares were up 35.2 points at 7,094.8 points and golds were off 0.3 points at 1,301.6 points.
De Beers was up 250 cents at 161 rand, Richemont was up 100 cents at 58.25 rand and Sasol was off 125 cents at 47.25 rand.
Share futures hardly budged throughout the day, also dampened by quiet trade ahead of the holidays.
Finishing the week a tad softer, contracts were seen trending firmer next week once volumes pick up.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,510/25 from 6,515, the industrial contract is at 8,115/22 from 8,130 and the gold contract is at 915/23 from 923.
